candidates.computation_change_reason: The header defines multiple parallel numeric columns (ambient Ca, effluent Ce, instream waste-concentration derivations, and several human-health/aquatic criteria). Which column is treated as the enforceable discharge limit for a given parameter and use classification changes limit selection and exceedance comparisons.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table column MQL
candidates.computation_change_reason: The MQL value may govern whether reported measurements are quantified enough for numeric compliance comparison, whether monitoring/reporting is expected at that detection level, and how sub-MQL or missing numeric results should be classified.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Molybdenum, dissolved
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row has a blank MQL and blank Ca/Ce cells but explicit zeros in derived instream columns and mixed finite/1E+100 criteria values. Interpreting blanks as absent limits, zero limits, or not-applicable changes whether a numeric limit applies, whether monitoring is required, and how missing or zero results are categorized.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Mercury, dissolved
candidates.computation_change_reason: The same pollutant row contains both 1E+100 sentinel values and finite acute (1.4) and chronic (0.77) aquatic criteria. Treating 1E+100 as non-operative versus as a numeric cap, and choosing among Ce, derived instream values, or endpoint-specific criteria, changes the applicable limit and exceedance outcome.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Mercury, total
candidates.computation_change_reason: Dissolved versus total mercury forms carry different finite criteria in the same table (e.g., human-health 2 vs 0.77 in other columns). Matching reported measurements to the correct form and criteria column changes which enforceable limit is selected.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Nickel, dissolved (P)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The '(P)' designation may mark a permit-priority or specially governed parameter, and the row mixes explicit zeros in instream columns with multiple finite endpoint criteria. Interpreting '(P)' and whether zeros are operative limits versus placeholders affects limit applicability and monitoring obligation scope.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Selenium, dissolved (P)
candidates.computation_change_reason: This selenium form is listed separately from the sulfate-conditioned variant and from total recoverable selenium, each with different criteria. Selecting the correct row for a reported selenium measurement changes applicable limits, monitoring expectations, and how unmatched or conditional cases are resolved.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Selenium, dis (SO4 >500 mg/l)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The row name embeds a sulfate-concentration condition (>500 mg/l) that gates which selenium criteria apply (e.g., irrigation 250 vs 130 in the non-conditioned row). Whether that condition is met changes limit selection, whether conditional monitoring was required, and how absent selenium results are interpreted.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Selenium, total recoverable
candidates.computation_change_reason: Total recoverable selenium carries different finite aquatic criteria (5 acute, 20 chronic) than the dissolved variants. Interpreting whether monitoring and limits attach to dissolved, total, or sulfate-conditioned forms changes obligation and compliance computations.

candidates.locator: page 5, section body, table row Zinc, dissolved
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row populates Ca, Ce, and multiple derived instream concentrations alongside several endpoint criteria with materially different magnitudes. Choosing effluent Ce, a derived instream value, or a specific human-health/aquatic criterion as the enforceable limit changes exceedance determinations.

The row lacks an MQL entry while still listing numeric criteria and zeros in instream columns. Interpreting the missing MQL as no monitoring expectation, as inherited default quantitation, or as unresolved evidence changes monitoring-obligation and missing-result classifications.
